name: ETF trend (Faber 10-month moving average, 5 ETFs)
sources: Faber, M., "A Quantitative Approach to Tactical Asset Allocation", Journal of Wealth Management, Spring 2007. SSRN abstract_id=962461 (papers.ssrn.com/sol3/papers.cfm?abstract_id=962461). CHECKED against the actual paper text on 2026-09-23 (WP8.2-style citation verification, done by hand, not yet the automated pipeline): confirmed real, confirmed the 10-month-SMA/month-end/long-or-cash rule as stated in rule_text below. See expected_ranges[0].note for what did NOT check out.

Reference implementation: SignalEngine crates/reference-rules::decide_etf_trend (weightsim_rules::adapters::EtfTrendRule over reference-rules), the same golden-tested Rust reimplementation cited on version 1, now the actual compiled rule this platform's fixed-rule replication endpoint runs and certifies against the embedded replication_ladder answer key (Amendment 11).
rule_text: Universe: SPY, EFA, IEF, DBC, VNQ. At each month-end (the last available trading day of the calendar month), for each ETF: if its month-end close is above the simple average of its last 10 month-end closes, INCLUDING the current month-end close, hold that ETF for the next month at 20% of the sleeve's equity; otherwise hold cash in its place (zero return). Rebalance monthly at the month-end close. A position decided at the close of day t earns returns from the next trading day's close-to-close return onward; a decision uses only data available at the close of the decision day. Long only, no leverage: maximum gross exposure is 100% of sleeve equity (5 x 20%). The reference implementation uses price-only closes (dividends not included), which understates the returns of income-paying ETFs.
reference_implementation: SignalEngine crates/reference-rules::decide_etf_trend, replayed against Massive daily bars (program/tests/fixtures/replication_ladder, Amendment 11, SHA-256 pinned) by weightsim_rules::ladder::replicate. Version pin: weightsim-rules 0.1.0 over reference-rules, Core rev bf05c19b.

notes: min_history_years is the history needed to compute the FIRST signal only (10 month-end closes); a meaningful backtest needs far more.
Whether live trading is wired for Alpaca (today: no, paper only) is a PLATFORM fact kept in PlatformCapabilities, not in this entry.

rebalance.detail: Decided at the close of the last bar of each calendar month (last_bar_of_month); the new target is first actionable on the first bar of the following month (operating_procedure.actionable_after), matching a live account's one-session decision-to-action delay (COUNCIL_ETF_TIMING_AND_CADENCE.md Ruling 4). Holidays are not modelled beyond the fixture's own trading calendar.

expected_ranges.source: stage1-record SCORECARD_PREREGISTRATION.md, Layer B: the author's deliberately wide sanity band (set 2026-09-20), NOT a published figure. Recomputed on version 2 by the platform's own certified fixed-rule replication (weightsim_rules::ladder::replicate against program/tests/fixtures/replication_ladder), not merely reimplemented independently as on version 1.
expected_ranges.note: CHECKED 2026-09-23 against the actual paper text (SSRN 962461, extracted via pypdf): the previously-cited figures 'Sharpe ~0.81 (1972-2005) and ~0.68 (2006-2025)' do NOT appear anywhere in the paper and are now known to be wrong, not merely unverified -- likely misattributed from an unrelated secondary source. What the paper actually reports for its 5-asset-class out-of-sample test (1973-2008, not 1972-2005/2006-2025): 'the timing model increased returns by approximately 20%, decreased volatility by 20%, improved the Sharpe Ratio by 0.20, and reduced the maximum drawdown by nearly 50%' versus buy-and-hold (relative improvements, not absolute Sharpe levels for the timing portfolio -- an absolute figure may exist in the paper's exhibit tables/charts, which did not extract as text and were not checked). The platform's own certified replication (net, certification_flat_10bps_per_side, price-only closes, 2017-07-03 to 2026-08-31): Sharpe 0.610475, CAGR 3.9059%, vol 6.6383%, max drawdown -9.1084%; equal-weight buy-and-hold of the same five ETFs: max drawdown -26.68%. Price-only closes omit dividends (predicted 1.5-2.5 percentage points of CAGR understatement -- see known_deviations). Post-publication decay (McLean-Pontiff, ~58%, still unverified) means a positive result is an upper bound.

expected_ranges.source: The platform's own certified fixed-rule replication (weightsim_rules::ladder::replicate, zero-cost gross run against program/tests/fixtures/replication_ladder), recomputed by check A6/A8 of the replication label derivation on every read -- WP9.9's gross_and_net_reported_check requires this paired _gross metric beside sharpe_net.
expected_ranges.note: Certified gross (zero cost, price-only closes, 2017-07-03 to 2026-08-31): Sharpe 0.644879, CAGR 4.1395%, vol 6.6318%, max drawdown -8.9726%. Gross is higher than net by the certification's flat 10 bps per-side accounting cost only (not a realised fill cost -- see known_deviations).

expected_ranges.source: stage1-record SCORECARD_PREREGISTRATION.md, Layer B (drawdown magnitude at most 25%, and shallower than equal-weight buy-and-hold of the same five ETFs).
expected_ranges.note: Drawdown is stated as a positive fraction, net of the certification cost. Certified replication over 2017-07-03 to 2026-08-31: 9.1084% versus 26.68% for equal-weight buy-and-hold of the same five ETFs. One window; not a guarantee.

known_deviations: Price-only closes: dividends are excluded from SPY, EFA, IEF, DBC and VNQ. Predicted to understate CAGR by roughly 1.5 to 2.5 percentage points versus the total-return series of IEF, VNQ and EFA in particular, which pay meaningful income.

Same-close fills in the certified replication: a decision made at a month-end close is filled at that same close. A live account acts one session later, at the next open (COUNCIL_ETF_TIMING_AND_CADENCE.md Ruling 4: the decision is first actionable on the following month's first bar and fills at that bar's open, per operating_procedure above).

No lot rounding or minimum tickets: the certified replication trades fractional, continuous weights every month-end. A live account is subject to each venue's lot sizes and minimum order tickets, which this replication does not model.

Single-vendor daily bars: all five instruments are priced from one vendor's (Massive) daily bars. No cross-vendor reconciliation of the pinned candles was performed beyond the fixture's own SHA-256 pin (program/tests/fixtures/replication_ladder/MANIFEST.json).

The certified net figure uses a flat 10 bps per-side accounting cost (cost_model_id certification_flat_10bps_per_side), a stated bookkeeping device for comparing gross and net results consistently across rules, not a claim about realised trading costs on any venue.
failure_regimes: Sideways or choppy markets where prices repeatedly cross the 10-month average (whipsaw). GENERAL property of moving-average trend rules; NOT measured in the local files.
Income-heavy periods: price-only data omits dividends and understates the returns of IEF, VNQ and EFA, so backtest and live total return differ.
Post-publication decay: published edges tend to shrink after publication (McLean-Pontiff ~58%, UNVERIFIED secondary figure); read results as upper bounds.

cost_profile.note: Turnover as a multiple of sleeve equity is NOT recorded in the local files. The platform's certified replication counted 99 asset-level signal flips over 9.160849 years (2303 observations at 251.3959 per year), about 10.8 per year across the five ETFs -- matching version 1's independent-reimplementation count exactly, since both count the same published rule against the same pinned prices. Monthly cadence keeps turnover low; ETF spreads on these five funds are small but were not measured here. The certified net result above uses the certification_flat_10bps_per_side accounting cost, not a measured spread/impact model.

retirement_rule: Flag to the inbox for a human decision (the agent may not remove it on its own) when any of: (a) the monthly fidelity check finds signal agreement with the compiled reference implementation below 0.98; (b) the sleeve's own replayed drawdown reaches the mandate's first drawdown rung; (c) realised net results over a full evaluation window fall outside the expected ranges above; (d) a later decay_check replication run against this same rule_hash fails. The window length and any numeric tolerance for (c) must be set by the owner before go-live; none is assumed here.
